meta.title: Task center
meta.description: Keeps parallel work in view: a "Task center" row above Settings at the sidebar foot lists every Session that is running or waiting for you, and macOS notifications tell you when one asks a question or finishes while you are elsewhere. Click the row to open the list grouped as Waiting for you, Running, and Finished in the last 30 minutes; each row shows the Session title, its project, and how long ago it changed. Click a row to open that Session. Finished Sessions appear only while they are unread and less than 30 minutes old, and opening one marks it read, so it disappears. When another Session starts waiting for an answer, approval, or plan review, or finishes, the plugin posts a macOS notification (via the system Notification API) titled with the reason and showing the Session and project; clicking it brings the app forward and opens the Session. Every listed Session notifies you, including the one on screen. If the system refuses notifications, a matching in-page card at the lower right is used instead. The switch at the panel foot keeps the sidebar's project order following the most recently active Session (on by default; turn it off to keep a manual order). The panel foot reports whether the system allows notifications; macOS lists an app under System Settings → Notifications only after its first request, which the first reminder makes. Every reminder is posted as a macOS notification; the system decides whether it becomes a banner, a Notification Center entry, or nothing while the app is frontmost. The in-page card is only used when the page has no notification permission. The panel foot shows the last reminder with its time and channel, so you can confirm the pipeline fired.
